reference: Bash metadata and documented pty contracts. Private regular-file descriptors independently fix the negative isatty and successful/duplicate-close outcomes. Terminal/session behavior remains deferred; no external GNU PTY API parity is claimed.
coverage: Bash type -t and type identify pty as an enabled shell builtin.
Bash help exposes the pty documentation and lists each public subcommand family.
Actual private-descriptor nonterminal classification, closure, duplicate-close error and descriptor parse rejection.
exclusions: No GNU command provides this loadable's PTY/session API; no operational parity oracle is available.

Session/TTY allocation, positive terminal classification, child PTY lifecycle and serial line-discipline behavior remain deferred. Only ordinary private-file descriptors are used by runnable operations.

cases.purpose: Bash type -t must classify the statically enabled pty loadable as a builtin.
Bash type must describe pty as a shell builtin, not as an external executable.
The Bash help entry must document every public subcommand family declared by the loadable.
cases.script:
doc=$(help pty)
for text in \
  'pty setsid' \
  'pty open-tty PATH' \
  'pty isatty FD' \
  'pty tty-name FD' \
  'pty foreground PGRP' \
  'pty close FD' \
  'pty spawn FDVAR PIDVAR CMD' \
  'pty waitpid PID' \
  'pty echo FD on|off' \
  'pty resize FD' \
  'pty set-ldisc LDISC DEVICE'; do
  case $doc in
    *"$text"*) ;;
    *) exit 1 ;;
  esac
done
printf 'all documented subcommands present\n'

cases.purpose: Exercise setsid, open-tty, and foreground against a controlled session and controlling terminal.
cases.reason: Never executed. Everything is observable with the existing PTY driver plus a trusted python3 helper (allowed in the VM) that creates an unattached PTY pair for the open-tty acquisition path. No new driver capability is required.

cases.purpose: Exercise isatty, tty-name, close, echo, and resize on a private PTY pair.
Exercise spawn and waitpid with bounded child output, exit status, and descriptor cleanup.
Exercise set-ldisc validation and line-discipline changes against an isolated serial endpoint.
cases.reason: Never executed. r1-r3 are ordinary unprivileged fixtures. r4-r5 sit behind the candidate's CAP_SYS_ADMIN check (pty.c 902-908) and need a real serial endpoint, because changing a PTY's line discipline away from N_TTY is not a meaningful serial test.

cases.purpose: The assigned isatty interface classifies a private regular-file descriptor as nonterminal.
Close an explicitly opened private descriptor and verify a second close fails while the file remains intact.
cases.script:
exec 9>ordinary
printf saved >&9
pty close 9
if pty close 9; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
printf 'second-close=%s\n' "$rc"
exec 9<ordinary
value=$(<ordinary)
[[ $value == saved ]]
exec 9<&-

cases.purpose: Reject a nonnumeric descriptor before closing anything.
